newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania president urges EU, NATO to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania president urges EU, NATO to parliament.

text.p: The president of the Baltic state of Lithuania urged the country's new parliament on Monday to keep pursuing the twin aims of European Union and NATO entry.
The new parliament is dominated by the country's resurgent right-wing parties, spearheaded by Lithuanian independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis.

President Algirdas Brazauskas urged deputies to do their best to integrate Lithuania into the EU and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, goals the country set itself after quitting the former Soviet Union in 1991.
"Membership in the European Union and NATO is a top priority of Lithuania's foreign policy," Brazauskas said in an address at the new parliament's first sitting.
"We should spare neither time nor efforts for the realisation thereof as it is a guarantor of our security and further development of democracy," Brazauskas added.
Landsbergis' Homeland Union Party won by a landslide in the elections and has formed a coalition with the Christian Democrats with 86 seats in the 141-seat parliament.
Lithuania and fellow Baltic states Latvia and Estonia are anxious to reintegrate with the West, having been cut off during the 50 years they were part of the former Soviet Union.
